why_hot: Pair-setup, pair-verify, and camera stream configuration call tlv.encode. Values longer than 255 bytes take the fragment loop, which allocates a new growing bytes object on every fragment (encoded = encoded + tag + b'\xff' + slice). The benchmark encodes one 65536-byte value (65536 % 255 == 1, so both full fragments and the remainder run) plus a short second TLV. The returned bytes are the TLV8 layout tests/test_tlv.py locks, so a lower allocation count has to keep that layout.

why_hot: Each HomeKit Data Stream frame serializes its header dict and its message dict through hds_protocol.encode, including dataSend packet lists. Every int, string, bytes, list, and dict allocates its own tag bytes and intermediate joins. The benchmark value nests a 32-packet list and a 16-key dict; writing those tags into one buffer returns the same payload bytes and the same decode() result.

why_hot: AccessoryEncoder.persist rewrites the state file when a client pairs and when the config number changes. json.dump's default separators are ', ' and ': ', so each comma and colon in the hex-encoded keys, client maps, and key material costs an extra space. The benchmark state is a fixed MAC, fixed Ed25519 key, accessories hash, and four paired clients. Compact separators are still JSON: json.load returns the same object, and load_into restores the same mac, keys, paired clients, permissions, accessories hash, and config version. TLV and HDS payload sizes are already the fragment layouts their tests lock, so this is the encode path whose document can shrink.
